note: Hand-written model card notes for the corrected-filter Tranco run. train/card.py adds them to public/models/clickables-v1.json.
summary: The model is experimental and switched off by default. Its suggestions are advisory and never change the score, the history or the report.

Earlier results were inflated by label leakage. The earlier training filter dropped rows from pages with delegated (document-level) click listeners only when their label was 0, and kept every positive. Counting the raw crawl by page type and label showed that it kept 8,691 positives from delegated pages and only 60 from other pages, while every negative it kept came from a non-delegated page, so the page type gave the label away. The filter now drops whole delegated pages, whatever their labels, and every number on this card comes from that corrected run.

There are only 60 trustworthy positives, from 13 websites. The test split has 6 of them, from 2 websites, so the 95% intervals below cover nearly the whole range from 0 to 1. This run cannot measure how good the model is.

No threshold reached 90% precision on the calibration websites, so the precision gate is not met ("not reached"). Separately from the ship gate, the app makes suggestions at an operating threshold chosen by one fixed rule: the threshold with the best F1 on the calibration websites (the test websites are never used to choose it). That threshold is 0.00064, because the model ranks the calibration positives no better than chance, so the best F1 comes from flagging almost everything. On the test websites it flags 2,074 of 2,608 elements: precision 0.3% (95% interval 0.0% to 0.5%) and recall 100% (6 of 6; 95% interval 100% to 100%). Every suggestion is labelled low confidence.
failurePatterns: The errors have not been reviewed by hand. errors.json holds samples taken at the operating threshold: 50 of the 2,068 false positives on the test websites; there are no false negatives. No recurring causes are claimed.
limitations: The Tranco top-1,000 crawl produced 1,407 page records; 879 pages were used. After every row from delegated pages was removed, 9,654 candidate rows from 136 websites remain, and only 13 of those websites have any click-only control. One website (capcut.com) has 32 of the 60.
All examples come from the Tranco crawl. The corpus has no Vue or Angular pages, and the results are not representative of other kinds of websites.
labelHandCheckMethod: Method (ml/README.md, step 2): labels/sheet.mjs drew 300 random labelled elements; labels/audit.mjs re-checked each one in the live page with Chrome's DevTools Protocol, reading the element's own listeners and React handlers, its ancestors' and any document-level (delegated) listeners, and marked it correct, wrong or unsure; labels/score.mjs counted the verdicts. The check is automated: an independent manual review by the owner has not been done.
labelHandCheckReading: This measures whether the labels are accurate, and that still holds after the filter change, because filtering removes rows but does not change any label. It does not fix the small number of positives: only 4 of the judged labels were positive, and the corrected corpus has only 60.
